components.gap: Argument / full treatment promised by its declared status (proved=annex:p15.binomial.most.powerful) not supplied for the explicit two-sided failure. The annex writes the p=3/4 bound (1/4)a+(3/4)b=(1/4)(a+b)+(1/2)b<=3/4 and its equality case (annex lines 260-269). The p=1/4 half, which the conclusion 'no test is most powerful simultaneously against p=1/4 and p=3/4' needs, is only 'the reversed calculation forces a=1,b=0 for its maximum power 3/4' (lines 270-272). The power (3/4)a+(1/4)b at p=1/4, its bound 3/4 under a+b<=1 and the equality case a=1,b=0 are never written. That is a 'similarly'-type step in place of an owed sub-proof.

components.gap: Argument / full treatment promised by its declared status (proved=annex:p15.confidence.test.inversion) is incomplete for the measurable converse. The statement's claim that integrating out u 'gives jointly measurable randomized tests' rests on annex lines 381-390, which only outline a monotone-class argument ('follows first for rectangle indicators, then for nonnegative simple functions and their monotone limits; the monotone-class extension covers the product sigma-field'). The outline lists its stages out of order and verifies none of them. It does not invoke the handbook's proved section-measure lemma (thm:p15-section-measures / thm:p15-tonelli, handbook/parts/p15/product-measures.tex 143-181). That lemma is stated for two sigma-finite factor measures, while Lambda x X carries none here, so even a citation would need adapting. A sketch counts as partial.

components.gap: Argument / full treatment promised by its declared status (proved=annex:p15.neyman.interval.construction) is incomplete for the interval reconstruction S(x)=[l(x),u(x)] cap R. Membership of a finite lower endpoint is proved (annex lines 439-444). Membership of a finite upper endpoint is only 'The same argument puts a finite u in S(x)' (lines 445-446). components.gap: Argument / full treatment promised by its declared status (proved=annex:p15.binomial.confidence.coverage) is incomplete for the claim 'The interval is exactly the inversion of the nonrandomized test' and for the acceptance of the upper root endpoint. The lower-endpoint equivalence is argued from strict monotonicity of T (annex lines 581-592). The upper-endpoint equivalence p>u_n(k) <=> F_{n,p}(k)<d (k<n) and the k=n case are only 'Similarly ...; for k=n, both are false' (lines 593-600). Neither the strict decrease of F_{n,p}(k) together with F_{n,u_n(k)}(k)=d, nor u_n(n)=1 together with F_{n,p}(n)=1, is written. The coverage bound (lines 609-621) uses the rejection event {F<d}, so it also rests on this unwritten half.

C007 is recorded covered as a definition, but its construction 'choose j in {0,...,n} and gamma in [0,1] with P(K>j)<=alpha<=P(K>=j)' never argues that such j exists or that the displayed gamma lies in [0,1]. Positivity of P_{p0}(K=j) for 0<p0<1 is also left implicit, and alpha is not quantified in the definition. thm:p15-likelihood-threshold proves existence of a threshold c for a general likelihood ratio, but no text maps c to the count threshold j. The C008 annex (lines 196-207) treats the test as given.

C006 is recorded covered. The lemma assumes stationarity of every variation. NP1933 p.300 (PDF p.13) instead derives stationarity from the best critical region minimizing the unconditioned P0(w)-kP1(w) of (17) on p.298, and then extends p0=kp1 'at every point on the complete boundary S'. Neither the minimum => stationary step nor the extension to the whole boundary is reproduced. The handbook explicitly limits itself to local stationarity and disclaims a Lagrange multiplier (body lines 150-153, annex lines 183-185), so this is recorded rather than failed.

Line numbers are PDF pages; PDF pp.8-14 = NP1933 pp.295-301, inside the cited extent pp.293-301. This material has no counterpart in the chapter: NP's likelihood criterion lambda=p0/p_Omega and its composite form with lambda<=C, (11)-(14) on p.295; the 'Good Critical Region' as an envelope and similar regions on p.298; the a-priori-probability remark and the relation of best critical regions to the likelihood principle, (29)-(30) on p.301. No queue component names these items and the scope notes were not opened (instruction), so this is not scored.

C001 uses type-I/type-II errors and a level-<=alpha most-powerful test. The source's own forms are 'errors of the first kind' and the 'second source of error', and a best critical region chosen among regions with P0(w)=eps exactly, as a family indexed by eps (NP1933 pp.296-297, PDF pp.9-10). These are not recorded at the definition. The exact-size variant appears only implicitly, in the c>0 clause of thm:p15-neyman-pearson (lines 114-115) and in annex line 124 ('indicator tests of equal size').

C013 fails on another ground; this is a separate note. The index set of the acceptance family is left implicit ('For a real target t'). Hypothesis (3), required for all finite a<b, and the conclusion S(x)=[l(x),u(x)] cap R presuppose A_t for every real t. If the target range is a proper subset of R, a section open at the edge of the range is excluded, although Neyman's condition (iv) (p.354, PDF p.23) quantifies only over parameter values.

Wording/correctness note, not scored: 'if c=0, a smaller size can attain the same power' holds only when P0(f1>0)<alpha. If P0(f1>0)=alpha, every most-powerful test must equal 1 a.e. on {f1>0} and so has size alpha. The annex (lines 102-105) argues only that the remaining size need not be spent.

Neyman's (20) (p.348, PDF p.17) requires equality for every theta1^0 and every value of the other parameters. The handbook identifies his coefficient with 1-alpha but does not say that his definition is the exact-coverage case of the chapter's 'at least 1-alpha'. That correspondence can be recovered only from the exact q of thm:p15-neyman-interval-construction.

'the integer gamma integral' is used without a reference to thm:p15-gamma-normalization (handbook/parts/p15/convolution-gamma-normal.tex), which proves Gamma(k+1)=k!. The alternative integration-by-parts justification is only described.
